verdict.rationale: Microsoft's FAQ documents App Lock, which requires the device PIN or biometric every time Authenticator is opened. It says this protects the one-time codes, app information, and settings, which matches the borrowed-phone scenario. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that App Lock works as described, and documentation of whether it is on by default or must be turned on (the docs only say "when App Lock is enabled").

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app itself locks behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose my codes

citations.quote: When App Lock is enabled, you'll be asked to authenticate using your device PIN or biometric every time you open Authenticator.
App Lock helps keep your one-time verification codes, app information, and app settings more secure.
